fdroid:at.clavierhaus.claviertuner.name: Clavier Tuner
fdroid:at.clavierhaus.claviertuner.summary: Piano tuning from the piano in front of you: measured, not assumed
fdroid:at.clavierhaus.claviertuner.description:
Clavier Tuner is a piano tuning app made by a piano tuner — free, open source, and built on one idea: the only truth about a string is a measurement of that string.
A4 ON THE STRING YOU CHOOSE
The first page sets the pitch: tap − or +, or slide a finger along the strip under them. Strike each string of A4 alone and its partials stand as strobes: a clean string's move together and stand still together, a false partial beats on its own. Take the cleanest as your reference.
MEASURE FIRST
Strike single strings with the others muted, any keys up to G6 in any order: eight at least, 10 to 15 spread up to G6 for the best result. From those strings the app measures the inharmonicity of your piano and works out where every note belongs, before you tune the first one. The stretch comes from this instrument, not from a table. Each key says when its measurement is complete.
TUNE BY THE STROBE
The app follows the key you strike and listens to the partial a tuner would listen to in that register. The strobe shows that partial against its target to a tenth of a cent, at 47 readings a second — a string that wobbles is shown wobbling. The string's other partials stand beside it, each in its own band: a clean string is one pattern that comes to a standstill, a false partial is the one out of step. When the strobe stands still, the note is in, and the app notes it. No wizard, no verdict dressed up as a number.
YOUR PIANO, YOUR PHONE
A line at the top shows what this tuning is tuned to — A4, the temperament octave, the octave types — and a tap on it changes them. Octave type and width per register (2:1 to 10:5, the double octave 4:1, the twelfth 3:1), the wound/plain break, the match window: the engine carries them as settings and the measurement decides the rest. The session is kept on the phone in one sealed file; continue tomorrow where you stopped. No account, no server, nothing leaves the phone. The microphone is read raw, with every effect switched off.
HONEST ABOUT WHAT IT IS NOT
Pitch raises are out of scope by design: a piano far from pitch needs a pitch raise first. Unisons are tuned by ear, as they should be.
OPEN
The whole engine is published, with its tests and the documents it is judged by. If you want to know how a number on the screen was made, you can read it.

-------------

- MQTT parameters
 - Host Name / IP address

 - Password

- Update parameters
 - Update cycle time [s]
 - OBD data items
 - Selection of subset of AndrOBD data items for display.

fdroid:dev.kokoro.tts.name: Kokoro Android system TTS driver
fdroid:dev.kokoro.tts.summary: Text-to-speech engine that speaks through your own Kokoro server
fdroid:dev.kokoro.tts.description:
A system text-to-speech engine (TextToSpeechService) for Android that speaks through
a Kokoro server, so any app that can read text aloud can use it.
It is not a plain HTTP client. Kokoro's hard limit is 510 phoneme tokens, and because
that counts the length of the IPA phoneme string rather than characters, a character
budget cannot enforce it: a 42-character Chinese sentence is 545 tokens, while English
prose of the same length is about 42. Text is therefore split on the device by a cost
model fitted to real Kokoro G2P output, and every split is verified lossless - the
same words, in the same order.
What it does:
* Splits text on the device, sized by estimated phoneme tokens rather than characters
* Trims the silence Kokoro pads around every chunk (50 ms before, 360 ms after)
* Inserts pauses at chunk joins, or none at all if the app you listen with already
 adds its own
* Starts speaking after a deliberately small first chunk, so turning a page begins in
 about a second instead of six
* Fetches the next chunk while the current one is still playing
* Fetches the voice list from the server, so every voice it offers is selectable
Requires a Kokoro server that you run yourself. Any OpenAI-compatible
/v1/audio/speech endpoint works; this was developed and measured against
Kokoro-FastAPI. The endpoint is configurable, so nothing is tied to one host, and
the app sends nothing anywhere except to the server you point it at.
Both http:// and https:// endpoints work, so a server behind a reverse proxy with a
certificate can be reached over TLS. The default is plain http:// because the usual
case is a Kokoro server on your own network.
No ads, no tracking, no accounts, no network access beyond your own server.

Hatari is an Atari ST/STE/TT/Falcon emulator for GNU/Linux, BSD, Mac OS X, Windows and
 other systems which are supported by the SDL library. The Atari ST was a 16/32 bit
 computer system which was first released by Atari in 1985. Using the Motorola 68000 CPU,
 it was a very popular computer having quite a lot of CPU power at that time. Unlike many
 other Atari ST emulators which try to give you a good environment for running GEM
 applications, Hatari tries to emulate the hardware of a ST as close as possible so that
 it is able to run most of the old ST games and demos. Hatari is open source software and
 is distributed under the terms of the GNU General Public License (GPL).
 Hatari supports the emulation of most of the ST and STE hardware, including some special
 tricks like raster interrupts, border effects and PSG sample sound. A joystick can be
 emulated with the cursor keys or with a real PC joystick. Hatari also features the
 possibility to "mount" a directory of the host system as a ST drive, or to use images
 from an original Atari's hard disk.
 Hatari is also able to emulate the additional hardware of the TT or Falcon machines,
 like the Videl video chip or the DSP 56001. However, note that TT and Falcon support are
 currently still in development and experimental.

firefox-addons:897889.name: Privacy Guard & Manager
firefox-addons:897889.summary: Easily control settings in your browser that affect your privacy.
firefox-addons:897889.description:
Privacy Guard & Manager is a browser addon that help you increase your privacy by adjusting few privacy settings in your browser. 
Simply open toolbar popup UI to see the list of available settings (19 items in total). Each setting has a drop-down list; click on the list to choose a desired value for that item. Once an item is changed, it will be saved to the memory automatically. Moreover, when you hover on any item within the toolbar popup UI, a description is shown at the bottom of the UI. Please read this description before changing any option. 
Note: you may see some disabled items in the toolbar popup UI. This is due to the browser version and OS limitations. These items may become available in future updates in your browser or OS.
Note: in order to report bugs, please fill the bug report form in the addon's homepage .

firefox-addons:2945298.name: Cookie Privacy Monitor
firefox-addons:2945298.summary: Monitor and manage cookies in real-time. Enhance privacy, reduce tracking, and protect against cross-site profiling. Works 100% offline.
firefox-addons:2945298.description:
Cookie Privacy Monitor 🔒
A comprehensive privacy-focused extension that gives you complete control over browser cookies. Monitor cookie activity in real-time, identify tracking cookies, and protect your privacy without relying on external services.
🚀 Key Features
 Real-time Monitoring 
- Track all cookie activity as you browse
- Visual risk scoring (low/medium/high) for each cookie
- Identify third-party and tracking cookies
 Privacy Protection 
- One-click tracker cookie removal
- Sandbox mode to isolate specific websites
- Prevent cross-site tracking and profiling
 Advanced Controls 
- Detailed cookie metadata inspection
- Category-based cookie management (trackers, third-party, session)
- Customizable monitoring preferences
🔒 Privacy First
 100% Offline : No data leaves your browser
 No Telemetry : Zero data collection or tracking
 Transparent : Open-source code for verification
 Local Storage : All data stays on your device
🛡️ Security Features
 Automatic detection of known tracking patterns
 Risk assessment based on multiple factors
 Safe cookie deletion with confirmation prompts
 No external dependencies or APIs
📊 For All Users
 Privacy-Conscious Users : Take back control of your online privacy
 Developers : Debug cookie behavior and understand tracking
 Organizations : Enhance employee privacy awareness
 Works seamlessly in the background without impacting browser performance.

firefox-addons:337037.name: Secure Password Generator
firefox-addons:337037.summary: Easy to use add-on to create random secure passwords.
firefox-addons:337037.description:
This add-on allows you to easily create random and secure passwords.
Right click on any password field on the webpage and select "Secure Password Generator"/"Generate password". Newly generated password will be inserted into selected field.
You can use "Insert previous password" context menu option if form requires you to repeat your password.

Overview

⚠️ This extension is NOT officially developed or supported by AgileBits (1Password). 
 A community preservation project created to maintain the legacy desktop app integration.

 Requires the 1Password Desktop Application (v4.x or compatible standalone version) .
 This extension simply allows continued use of software you already own.
Why This Extension?
When AgileBits discontinued support for the classic 1Password browser extension, many users were left relying on their standalone desktop vaults .
This port ensures that those users can continue using their existing software with:
 Future compatibility through Manifest V3 compliance
 Preserved functionality for standalone desktop licenses
 No cloud dependency — fully offline operation

✅ Desktop App Integration 
 Native messaging connection to the 1Password desktop app
 Secure access to local vaults
 No cloud or online account required
✅ Auto-Fill & Form Detection

 Works on all HTTP/HTTPS sites
✅ Browser Integration 
 Toolbar button for quick access
 Context menu options
 Keyboard shortcut support
 Tab-level security control
✅ Manifest V3 Compliance 
 Future-proof service worker architecture
 Modern permission model
 Compatible with Firefox 109.0+ 
✅ Security & Privacy 
 Private/incognito mode support
 Secure native messaging protocol
 No telemetry, analytics, or data collection
 All credentials remain local
Technical Improvements (v4.7.5.90 MV3)
 ✅ Migrated from Manifest V2 to Manifest V3
 ✅ Replaced deprecated browserAction API with action 
 ✅ Converted background page to service worker
 ✅ Added polyfills for legacy compatibility
 ✅ Introduced NoLegacy community branding
Installation Requirements
Prerequisites
 1Password Desktop App (v4.x or compatible standalone version) 
 Must be installed and properly configured
 Local vault must be accessible
 Valid 1Password License 
 A legitimate AgileBits license is required
 Works with both standalone and subscription accounts
 Firefox Browser 
 Version 109.0 or newer
 Developer Edition or Nightly recommended for unsigned builds

 This project serves purely as a compatibility bridge , not a crack or bypass.
 A valid AgileBits license is required to use 1Password features.
 The project fully respects all intellectual property rights.
Purpose

firefox-addons:2809511.name: Password Paster
firefox-addons:2809511.summary: Paste password in those website's input field where Ctrl+V doesn't functions
firefox-addons:2809511.description:
Frequently, we encounter websites that restrict pasting within their password input fields, like the login pages of banking sites. This compels us to manually input the password, which can be even more laborious when dealing with lengthy passwords from a password manager. Moreover, certain websites necessitate entering the password twice during sign-up, demanding a repetitive manual entry. This is where this extension becomes useful.
How to use
- Choose the website's input field.
- Launch the extension.
- Input the password into the extension's designated field.
- Click the "Paste" button.
- And just like that, the password will be populated in the corresponding field on the website.

apple-macos:1667869674.description:
Prepare for CFA Levels I–III, GARP FRM, FINRA SIE and Series 7. Work through an investment question, analyze a case or draft a written response, then compare your reasoning with the explanation.
Try one free practice session per exam bank. Your session draws from a small selection of questions or cases. Items can repeat, and any previous practice session in that bank counts. A subscription or an active pass unlocks further practice and all timed mock exams, both short and full-length. Your saved answers and explanations remain available after the free session.
Questions, cases and written answers
The full library includes 205+ study banks with 222,000+ standalone questions, 2,500+ vignette cases and 2,900+ essay cases. Separate exam versions and companion formats count as individual study banks.
CFA Level I covers the 2027 curriculum for exams from February 2027. At Level II, answer questions about a shared case. At Level III, choose Portfolio Management, Private Markets or Private Wealth, then select item sets or written practice. For CFA and supported CISI written banks, draft an answer and score it against an editorial rubric.
Choose your next topic
Study today suggests a topic based on saved practice and recent results where available. Choose your own topic or resume an unfinished practice session saved on this device. When you review an attempt, use the question overview to find marked items and the answer explanation panel to see the reasoning. Compare topic results across saved attempts.
Find your exam
In the United States, choose FINRA SIE and Series exams, NASAA, CPA, CFP, CMA Part 1 selected-response practice or the SAFE MLO National Test. Canadian banks cover CSC, CIRO CIRE/RSE, IFC, LLQP, RIBO and CIP C11. United Kingdom options include CISI, selected CII units and FSRE (FRE1/FRE2).
Other options include GARP FRM Parts I and II, RAI, SCR and FRR, plus ACAMS CAMS and CGSS.
More regional banks include
• ASIC Financial Adviser Exam (Australia)
• CA ANZ Tax NZ written practice (New Zealand)
• NISM V-A, V-D and Series VIII Equity Derivatives (India)
• AMF General in English (France)
• QFA Regulation module (Ireland)
• FSCA RE1, RE3, RE4 and RE5, plus SAIFM RPE equity, bond and derivatives markets, financial markets and regulation (South Africa)
• HKSI LE Paper 1 (Hong Kong)
• CMFAS RES5 (Singapore)
• SIDC SCLE Module 6 (Malaysia)
• CME-1A Saudi-route companion (English syllabus V19)
Classic CSC Exams 1 and 2 have separate banks from the CSC1 Core Readiness and CSC2 Future Readiness companions. CII R06 and CPA Canada CFE Day 1 companions use case-based questions.
Full library access
Choose a one-time pass or a subscription to open every Finance Mastery bank while active. Passes expire at the end of their term. Subscriptions renew unless canceled. View plans and prices in the app. Use the same account on supported Apple devices and at MasteryExamPrep.com. Internet access is required. Content is in English.

- Seven-day forecast with daily detail
- Tap any day for a 24-hour forecast
- Rain radar and cloud/UV map layers
- Fahrenheit and Celsius switch
- Save recent cities and use current location

apple-itunes:6784015213.name: CloudSurf
apple-itunes:6784015213.description:
CloudSurf is the workspace app for iPhone and iPad by CloudSurf Software LLC. Surfy, the built-in assistant, turns a chat into something real: describe an app, a site or a document, and Surfy builds it. Chat to app.
BUILT FOR IPHONE DUO
CloudSurf works in every pose. Closed portrait and closed landscape: the cover screen carries the whole app with a rail of tabs beside the status cluster. Open landscape: Tasks and Messages sit beside the Desk — the list on the left, what you opened on the right — and Cloud and your docs take the whole screen. Open portrait: a full-height page. Tabletop: folded halfway, the top half is the screen with a dock above the hinge and the bottom half a keyboard and trackpad — a little computer in your pocket, with a pointer that clicks everything. Appearance is System, Light and Dark, and Dark is Surf Dark, CloudSurf's navy.
THE FIVE TABS
• Surfy — the home tab: your conversation with Surfy, ready the moment the app opens. Say what you want made and Surfy writes the doc, builds the app or site, and shows you as it works.
• Cloud — what you make and keep, newest first, with the kinds from your workspace: Apps, Domains, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Notes, Images, Videos, Audio, Files, Posts, Starred and Games. An app's page holds its web page, its code repositories (Code) and its look (Look): the style, the accent, the fonts, Light, Dark or Auto.
• Tasks — what needs to be done, on its way to Done, with a search field and the status and source menus beside the title.
